By the Court:-
1. Heard the parties.

2. This criminal miscellaneous petition has been filed invoking the jurisdiction of this Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C. with a prayer to quash the entire criminal proceeding in connection with Mango P.S. Case No. 257 of 2020, corresponding to G.R. No.875 of 2021 in which police submitted charge sheet inter alia against the petitioner for having committed the offences punishable under Section 406/420 of Indian Penal Code and vide order dated 10.05.2021, the learned Judicial Magistrate 1st Class, Jamshedpur has taken cognizance of the said offences.

sentences.text: The brief fact of the case is that the complainant entered into an agreement to purchase a piece of land.

The complainant paid some amount to the co-accused persons who have been arraigned as accused nos.2 to 4 in the complaint which upon being referred to police under Section 156 (3) Cr.P.C. the said Mango P.S. Case No.
257 of 2020 has been registered.

4. It is the case of the complainant-informant that though he is ready to pay the remaining amount to the petitioner also but the petitioner is neither receiving the amount nor delivering the possession of the land.

5. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that admittedly there is no entrustment of any money or property to the petitioner and there is no allegation against the petitioner of inducing the complainant-informant in any manner to part with the property.

It is further submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the informant failed to pay the sale consideration to the petitioner and others at the rate of Rs.3,00,000/- per khatha i.e. in total Rs.78,00,000/- within three months from the date of sale agreement dated 22.01.2019 but as the informant failed to pay the said amount therefore, vide legal notice dated 03.06.2019, the petitioner and others have revoked the agreement for sale and for wreaking vengeance, this false case has been foisted against the petitioner.

It is next submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the dispute between the parties is basically a civil dispute and even if the allegation made against the petitioner are considered to be true in their entirety still neither the offence punishable under Section 406 of Indian Penal Code nor the offence punishable under Section 420 of Indian Penal Code is made out against the petitioner.
Hence, it is submitted that the prayer as made in this criminal miscellaneous petition be allowed.

6. Learned Special Public Prosecutor and the learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 on the other hand opposes the prayer to quash the entire criminal proceeding and submits that the petitioner has induced the complainant to give more than Rs.40,00,000/- which has been received by the co-accused persons.
Hence, it is submitted that this criminal miscellaneous petition being without any merit be dismissed.

7. Having heard the submissions made at the Bar and after going through the materials in the record, it is pertinent to mention here that it is a settled principle of law that a breach of contract does not give rise to criminal prosecution for cheating unless fraudulent or dishonest intention is shown right at the beginning of the transaction.

Merely on the allegation of failure to keep up promise will not be enough to initiate criminal proceedings as has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Sarabjit Kaur v. State of Punjab reported in (2023) 5 SCC 360.
8.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is also a settled principle of law that to constitute the offence of cheating under Section 420 of Indian Penal Code there has to be any deception played at the very Sanjit Mahato @ Sanjit Mahato vs The State Of Jharkhand on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46918475/
2 inception.

entities.text: Sanjit Mahato @ Sanjit Mahato vs The State Of Jharkhand
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
If the intention to cheat has developed later on the same cannot amount to cheating as has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Uma Shankar Gopalika vs. State of Bihar & Anr. reported in (2005) 10 SCC 336, paragraph no. 6 of which reads as under :-
6. Xxxx xxxx xxxx

entities.text: Uma Shankar Gopalika vs. State of Bihar & Anr. reported in (2005) 10 SCC 336
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is well settled that every breach of contract would not give rise to an offence of cheating and only in those cases breach of contract would amount to cheating where there was any deception played at the very inception.
If the intention to cheat has developed later on, the same cannot amount to cheating.

In the present case it has nowhere been stated that at the very inception there was any intention on behalf of the accused persons to cheat which is a condition precedent for an offence under Section 420 IPC."
(Emphasis supplied)

9. Now coming to the facts of the case, there is absolutely no allegation against the petitioner of having any intention to deceive the complainant-informant since the beginning of the transaction between them.
Nor any specific allegation is there against the petitioner that he ever cheated and thereby induced to the complainant to part with any money or other property.

Thus, under such circumstances, this Court is of the considered view that even if the entire allegation made against the petitioners are considered to be true in their entirety still the offence punishable under Section 420 of Indian Penal Code is not made out.

10. So far as the offence punishable under Section 406 of Indian Penal Code is concerned, the essential ingredients to constitute the offence punishable under Section 406 of Indian Penal Code are as follows:-
(i) There must be an entrustment;
(ii) There must be dishonest misappropriation or conversion to one's own use, or use in violation of a legal direction or of any legal contract as has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Ram Narayan vs. CBI reported in (2003) 3 SCC 641.
11.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Now coming to the facts of the case, admittedly, there was no entrustment to the petitioner.

12. Under such circumstances, this Court is of the considered view that even if the entire allegation made against the petitioner are considered to be true in their entirety still the offence punishable under Section 406 of Indian Penal Code is not made out.

13. In view of the discussions made above, as neither the offence punishable under Section 406 of Indian Penal Code nor the offence punishable under Section 420 of Indian Penal Code is made out against the petitioner, hence, this Court is of the considered view that continuation of the criminal proceeding will amount to abuse of process of law and this is a fit case where the entire criminal proceeding in connection with Mango P.S. 14. Accordingly, the entire criminal proceeding in connection with Mango P.S. Case No. 257 of 2020,
corresponding to G.R. No.875 of 2021 including the order dated 10.05.2021 passed by the Judicial Magistrate 1st Class, Jamshedpur is quashed and set aside qua the petitioner only.
15. In the result, this criminal miscellaneous petition is allowed.
